copy.blurb:
Ecuador face Germany on Thursday, evening UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a wide disagreement by the engine's standards on the Ecuador side, +10.1pp.

Public Elo rates Germany 110 points higher than the other side (Ecuador 1790, Germany 1900). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Ecuador to win at 27%, the draw at 23%, and Germany to win at 50%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Ecuador on the win side reads 27%.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Ecuador to win at 16%, the draw at 22%, and Germany to win at 60%. The Ecuador side trades at 16% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +506. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 27%, +10.1pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Ecuador side that lower bound is 23% — +6.0pp clear of the market's 16%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the Ecuador side specifically.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 34 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read. Two outlets covered the build-up this week — BBC Sport (football): "Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer comes out of international retirement to be named in Germany's squad for the 2026 World Cup, with…"; The Guardian (football): "Yes I plan with [Neuer as No 1]"
drivers: The +10.1pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Ecuador side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Ecuador side still clears the Pick threshold.

editorial_citations.quote: Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer comes out of international retirement to be named in Germany's squad for the 2026 World Cup, with manager Julian Nagelsmann saying the 40-year-old will be his team's number one for the tournament.
Yes I plan with [Neuer as No 1]
The main task was to nominate the best three keepers. So we decided that these three are part of that. We contacted Manuel and asked him if he wanted to play for the national team again.

copy.summary: The model thinks Ecuador are mispriced. Our number reads 27% on the home side; the market reads 16%. The +10.1pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Ecuador v Germany · the model leans Ecuador
